declarations.documentation:
Register one @spec@ as desired and mint its durable name `<kind>-<n>`. The next number and the write
happen in one critical section of the shared place's serial domain (a `store.exclusive` performed inside
a `store.shared`), because minting is a read-modify-write and two callers deciding at the same instant
would otherwise mint the same name. The name is returned for the caller to fork under, so the store
wants the fiber before the fiber exists; nothing here forks, and @spec@ crosses as `unknown`.
declarations.name: register

declarations.documentation:
Forget the spec named @name@ — the one door out of the desired set, and a decision: someone said this
should stop being wanted. Nothing here reacts to a fiber's death, so a fiber that crashed, was cancelled
or simply ended leaves its spec alone and the next boot brings it back. Total in both directions a
caller cannot control: a name with no stored spec is a harmless no-op, and a name that is not a legal
store segment is ignored rather than turned into a key; a single-key delete takes no critical section.
declarations.name: forget

declarations.checkedType: agent(root: string, validate: agent(value: unknown) -> (null | T2)) -> sweep_result[T2] with throw[validation_error] | shared
declarations.documentation:
Sweep the desired set: read every stored spec, hand it to @validate@, keep the ones that parse and
delete the ones that do not, answering with both halves. This is the boot move — a hand-edited cell or a
spec shape changed across a deploy may neither fail a boot nor sit in the store forever. @validate@ is
the caller's own total parser (`prelude.catch` around `json.validate[Spec]`, folding the error arm to
`null`) and its row is fixed to nothing, so a validator that throws or reaches the network will not
type-check here. T is read off the callback's result and inference does not reach into an argument's
return type, so instantiate it: `fleet.sweep[my_spec](...)`. What is dropped is a row nobody can read —
never a judgement about the fiber — and @dropped@ is returned rather than reported because the sentence
belongs to the app.
declarations.name: sweep

parameters.documentation: The registry root under the shared place.
parameters.label: root

parameters.documentation: The caller's total validator: the parsed spec, or `null` for a value that no longer conforms.
parameters.label: validate

declarations.signature: agent sweep[T extends unknown](root: string, validate: agent(value: unknown) -> T | null) -> sweep_result[T] with store.shared | prelude.throw[json.validation_error]

declarations.documentation:
Plan the reconcile: the pure difference between the desired names and the live ones. @missing@ is
desired-and-not-live — what a boot forks; @orphans@ is live-and-not-desired — what a reconciler would
stop. Nothing is read, written or acted on, and input order is preserved. @orphans@ describes this
fleet only when @live@ holds this fleet's fibers alone: a nursery also carrying sources, crons or
queued mail lists every one of them as an orphan, so pass a narrowed live list, or use @missing@, which
is well defined whatever else is running.
declarations.name: plan

parameters.documentation: The durable names in the desired set.
parameters.label: desired

desired.description: The durable names in the desired set.

gap: The difference between the two sets, as `plan` computes it: what is desired and not live, and what is
live and not desired. Nothing here is acted on — a gap is a statement about two lists.
